# Music Scales App

This is an app for music scales. We don’t have all scales. I might extend this to chords in the future.

## How to Use

### Section 1: Downloading

If you have the folder, then go to it in Google Drive and Click the 3 Dots (⋮), then click “Download”. Like:

![][image1]

When you click “Download”, you should see a ZIP file named something like “Music Theory-DATE-1-001.zip”. Unzip the contents to see a folder called “Music Theory”.

Drag that to somewhere you won’t forget.

### Section 2: Opening the App

Double click on the “Music Theory” folder. It should look like:

![][image2]

If you see a folder called “.git”, feel free to remove it.

Then double click on “index.html”&nbsp;

### Section 3: Using the App

The app is relatively simple to use. When double clicking index.html, you should see something like:

![][image3]

There are two buttons: “Find Scales” and “Practice Scales”. These next few sections will explain its purpose and how to use them.

#### Section 3.1: Find Scales

This side of the app looks like this:

![][image4]

There’s two dropdowns. The first one (the left) is the scale type. These are the types you can use:

* Major (Ionian)  
* Natural Minor (Aeolian)  
* Harmonic Major  
* Harmonic Minor  
* Pentatonic Major  
* Pentatonic Minor  
* Melodic Major  
* Melodic Minor  
* Dorian  
* Phrygian  
* Lydian  
* Mixolydian  
* Locrian

The other one (the right) is used to show how you want to visualize it. Note:

* For Treble and Bass Clef, the positions of the \#/b signs aren’t correct.  
* For Treble and Bass Clef, the clefs are just “&” for Treble and “?” for Bass.  
* For Treble and Bass Clef, it doesn’t play the octave  
* For Fretboard, You might not see all the 2 octaves for all scale, because it only goes to the 4th fret for visibility

Below the dropdowns, there should be a piano looking interface. This lets you decide the I (or tonic) of the scale.

Then, at the bottom (you might have to scroll a bit), click “Find Scale” to see the visualization.

Below the visualization should be the note names.

Let’s try to find Ab Lydian with this app.

1. Choose the type (Lydian)  
2. Choose the visualization (I will choose tablature)  
3. Choose the root (G\#/Ab)

It should look like:

![][image5]

#### Section 3.2: Practice Scales

This side of the app should look like:

![][image6]

To use this app, it’s really simple.

Simply click on the skill set and get your scale.

If you don’t know a scale, either use the Find Scales side of our app or reroll for another scale (Reroll button).

You can also reroll if a scale is too simple.

For example, choosing an “Advanced” scale can give:

![][image7]

The scale you should practice is **below** the Reroll button.

### Section 4: Final Words

1. This is a music theory web app. This is **not** a DAW. It can produce sounds, but it sucks as a music composition tool.  
2. This is made for fun. I’m aware there exists many apps that can do what this app does but better and there’s more things, but I just wanted to practice coding.  

### Section 5: Technical Stuff (For anyone that cares about how it works or how it’s made)

This was made with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with WebAudio and Canvas API.

Without breaks, this was made in 4 days.

\~80-90% JS, \~6% CSS, \~4% HTML

This is mainly human-made, but there was some AI assistance. (Essentially, it’s not vibe coded, but I did use AI to help)

* 3 HTML Files  
* 3 CSS Files  
* 5 JavaScript Files

This project did use Git for version control. Source Code is on GitHub.

User name: TrevorDaBest. Repository Name: Music Theory.
